# RQ-PHX-RECONCILEINTENTWORLD09SPK1 bridge notes

Preserves **only the intent-to-world-model integration** of retained original PR #4235
(retained head SHA `80f1d451949b26685cafa3ffa973d3933901634d`). This does not reconcile the
rest of #4235 and does not close it.

## Preserved slice
Reference-only reads of #4235's `src/core/world/{project,read,types}.ts`; nothing cherry-picked or restored.
Reimplemented against master's `src/core/intent/summary.ts` (`IntentSummary`, `intentSummary`):

- `project.ts`: pure `intents?: IntentSummary | null` input. `present: false`/null/invalid counts are unknown; an observed valid empty ledger is zero. Shipped is never inferred from merged. Stale records become blind spots `intents.stale.<id>` (freshness `stale`), deduplicated by id and sorted with all other spots. Only stable ids are exported, never titles. Guidance names `ashlr fleet intent-sweep` (`--apply` refreshes locally).
- `read.ts`: `buildWorldModel` calls read-only `intentSummary({ nowMs })` (honors `ASHLR_RUNS_DIR` and the builder's `nowMs`); a throw yields unknown without dropping other facts. Disk cache without `intents` is rejected rather than shown as zeros.

  - Pins are deduped by kind+ref. At most 50 are kept and the oldest is dropped.
  - The title is capped at 160 characters and the ref at 512. Both must be a single line.
  - Writes are atomic through the existing `writePrivateFileAtomically` (exclusive temp file, mode 0600, fsync, rename).
  - A ref or title that `scrubSecrets` would change is **refused**, not redacted. Only refs are stored, never file contents.
  - A damaged store raises an error and is never silently reset.
- `src/cli/fleet-library-pins.ts` (new): `ashlr fleet library-pins [--json]`, `add --kind --ref --title [--json]`, `remove <id> [--json]`.
- `src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts`: exactly one line added. Note: master's registry is out of sync with `scripts/gen-fleet-registry.mjs --check` (`intent-evidence`, `intent-summary` are missing). I left that alone per the one-line rule.
- `src/core/verse/library-pins-api.ts` (new) + one mount line in `verse-api.ts`: `GET/POST /api/verse/library/pins`, `DELETE /api/verse/library/pins/<id>`.
  - The dispatch + `passesMutationGate` handling is copied from `fleet-holds-api.ts`, and unknown body keys are refused.
  - POST also accepts `{remove: id}`. The web client's `apiDelete` sends no `Content-Type`, so `passesMutationGate` would answer 415 to it. The pane therefore unpins via POST. **Follow-up:** the same 415 likely affects `leader/thread-data.ts` directive retirement through `apiDelete`. Worth a separate job to set `Content-Type: application/json` on DELETE in `client.ts`.
- `src/web-ui/routes/verse/library/LibraryPins.tsx` (new): `libraryPinsQuery` (a 404 from an older server hides the toggles), `PinToggle`, and `PinnedGroup`. The group sits at the top of the pane and renders only when pins exist.
- `LibraryPane.tsx`: +6/−2. Adds a pin toggle on memory cards and bus rows, and the Pinned group at the top.
- `src/core/fleet/context-pack.ts`: `buildContextPack` has a clean sections list. When pins exist, it appends a `pinned-by-mason` section with `{kind, title, ref}` for the newest 10 pins. The section goes last, so the byte budget trims pins before existing fleet state. An unreadable store adds nothing and never fails the pack. The section applies to every job/lane pack, not only the Leader's.

## Tests (new)
- `test/library-pins.test.ts`, 8 tests:
  - store: add/dedupe/cap/remove, atomic write leaves no temp file, mode 0600, rejection of secret-shaped ref and title, damaged store
  - API: pin, list, unpin through POST and DELETE; refusals for a missing token (401), dispatch off (404), an unknown key (400) and a secret ref (400)
  - context pack: the section is present with pins and absent without
- `test/fleet-library-pins-cli.test.ts`: shape of `--json` list output, add then remove, bad input and help (2 tests).
- `src/web-ui/routes/verse/library/LibraryPins.test.tsx`: the toggle POSTs a pin and an unpin with the mutation token, the Pinned group renders only with pins, and toggles are hidden when the route returns 404 (3 tests).

## Commands run
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/library-pins.test.ts test/fleet-library-pins-cli.test.ts test/fleet-context-pack-reconcile-09snu1.test.ts`: 3 files, 13/13 pass (after the rebase).
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run --config vitest.config.web.ts src/web-ui/routes/verse/library/`: 7 files, 28/28 pass, including the existing LibraryPane suites.
- `npx --no-install tsgo ...`: tsgo is not installed (E404). Fell back to `npx --no-install tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`: **exit 0**.
- `npx eslint <changed files>`: **could not run**. `node_modules/eslint` in this worktree has no `lib/` (`Cannot find module '../lib/cli'`). I did not reinstall it. Merge Gate lint should cover it.

## Size
- 11 files, +590/−2. Non-test code is about 355 lines and tests are 237.
- This is over the ~400-line guide. The context-pack step is only 4 lines, so dropping it would not bring the change under budget. I kept it because it is the acceptance path ("visible in the Leader's context pack").

## Known limits
- Add and remove are read-modify-write with no lock, so a CLI write and an app write at the same instant could lose one pin. The atomic rename means the file is never torn.

# RQ-PHX-IDEASQUEUEACTION09: Ideas pane "Draft job" / "Draft together"

## What changed
- `src/core/web/ideas-draft-route.ts` (new): `POST /api/ideas/draft`, body `{ideaIds: 1..8, confirmCollisions?}`, returns `{draftId, collisions, written, existing}`.
  - Writes through the existing `writeDropJob` (drop-job-writer.ts); nothing writes ready.tsv, router-queue.md or the drop folder directly.
  - Draft id is `IDEA` + 12 hex of sha256 over the sorted idea ids, so the same set is idempotent (second click: `existing: true`, same id). A batch writes ONE draft whose goal lists each idea (title, repo, rationale, source/id/score).
  - Collisions are computed BEFORE the write (`extractJobPaths` + `readQueuedPathClaims` + `queuedCollisions`, the `draft-check --queued` logic). A colliding draft is held (`written: false`) until resent with `confirmCollisions: true`, so they are visible before it queues.
  - Same gate as other mutation routes: `--allow-dispatch`, `x-ashlr-token`, JSON content type. Backlog text is scrubbed/clipped; the writer's denied-content validation gives 422; queue-full gives 507.
- `src/core/web/api.ts`: 7 lines to mount the route beside `/api/backlog`.
- Ideas pane: `IdeaDraftChip.tsx` (new: post helper + chip), `IdeasPane.tsx` (per-idea button, checkboxes, "Draft together", chip), `ideas-model.ts` (`IdeaRow.id`), `ideas.module.css`.
- Tests (new): `test/ideas-draft-route.test.ts` (6), `src/web-ui/routes/verse/ideas/IdeasPane.draft.test.tsx` (4).

## Findings to know
- The task said draft verbs are a writer; `fleet draft-check` and the MCP draft tools are actually read-only checks. The real writer is `drop-job-writer.ts`, which is what I reused. Drafts are therefore drop jobs and are picked up by the sweep once written.
- The drop writer only emits `repo=phantom` jobs. Ideas from other repos are drafted as phantom-lane jobs with the target repo named in the goal text; a repo-aware path needs the writer to change (out of scope).
- Remote/phone gateway policy was not touched; the route is local-dashboard only.

title: bridge: RQ-PHX-COMMSCONFIRMDESK09
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-PHX-COMMSCONFIRMDESK09` (pool: claude), single commit on base `85b575959`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# RQ-PHX-COMMSCONFIRMDESK09: one-click, human-only Comms confirm

## What changed

- **NEW `src/core/comms/comms-confirm.ts`**
  - `readCommsLimits(configDir)` returns `{ state, limits, digest, confirmedAt }`.
    - `limits` holds `[team].identities` from `agent-network.toml` (who the transports may message without asking each time), their channels, and every other `comms.toml` setting flattened to `key = value`.
    - The state is `unknown` when `comms.toml` is missing, unreadable, malformed, or has a non-boolean `confirmedByMason`.
  - `confirmCommsLimits(configDir, { limitsDigest, confirmedAt })` refuses when:
    - the file is missing (it never creates it);
    - the file is malformed;
    - the digest no longer matches (`digest-mismatch`);
    - the bytes changed between read and swap (`changed`).
  - It edits only the top-level `confirmedByMason` / `confirmedAt` lines (or inserts them) and keeps comments, CRLF and every other byte.
  - It re-parses the result and refuses unless every non-confirmation setting is identical, so no limit can change here.
  - It writes `comms.toml.bak` (mode 0600), then writes the new file to a temp file, fsyncs it and renames it over the original.
  - The digest is `sha256:<hex>` of the canonical limits: all of `comms.toml` except the two confirmation keys, plus the team allowlist. The `sha256:` prefix is needed because the public-JSON secret scrubber redacts a bare 64-hex string, which would make a plain digest impossible to send back.
  - Directory: `~/.ashlr`, resolved with `realHome()`. This is what `imessage-teammate-transport.ts` and `send-gate.ts` read. The brief said `~/.phantom/agents/comms.toml`, but the code reads `~/.ashlr/comms.toml`, so I followed the code.
- **NEW `src/core/web/comms-confirm-route.ts`**: `GET|POST /api/verse/comms/confirm`. It is registered in `src/core/web/api.ts`, which is not in CODEOWNERS, next to `/api/verse/feedback` and before the `/api/verse/*` catch-all.
  - GET only reads. It sits behind the existing read-session boundary in `server.ts`.
  - POST is the only writer. The checks run in this order:
    1. `ctx.allowDispatch`, otherwise 404.
    2. Any `Authorization` header is refused with 403. This covers the Verse turn's MCP bearer.
    3. Same origin: `Origin` must equal `http://<Host>` (403 otherwise), and `Sec-Fetch-Site`, if sent, must be `same-origin`.
    4. `passesMutationGate`: the `x-ashlr-token` check plus the JSON content-type check (401/415).
    5. The body must carry a `sha256:` digest (400 otherwise).
  - The route sets `confirmedAt` from the server clock. It never takes it from the client.
- **NEW `src/web-ui/routes/verse/comms-confirm/CommsConfirmCard.tsx` (+ `.module.css`)**: the "Confirm Comms limits" item.
  - It shows, in plain words, who the agent may message unprompted, the channels, and the other settings, or "none, so comms.toml sets no daily cap".
  - It has one "Confirm these limits" button. The button is disabled without the mutation hold and while posting.
  - After a click it shows "Confirmed at <time>".
  - It renders nothing when `comms.toml` is absent, unknown or already confirmed.
  - It is mounted in `NeedsYouDrawer.tsx` on the All and Approvals splits as a single item. No new `*.pane.tsx`.
- `docs/IMESSAGE.md`: one sentence pointing to the card.
- No MCP tool or CLI verb was added. A test asserts that `confirmCommsLimits` is called only from the route.

The transports call `parseCommsConfirmation` on every send check (`approvedTeammateHandle`, `readLocalSendPolicy`, owner-channel), so they pick up the change on the next check without a restart.

## The gate I reused, and why it is human-only

It is the same gate as the Needs-you resolve route (`src/core/verse/agent-bus-api.ts`) and every Verse POST: `ctx.allowDispatch` plus `passesMutationGate` from `src/core/web/api.ts`.

- The mutation token is random for each server start. It is held in memory only: by the desktop app (`--desktop-token-handoff` private stdout handshake) or printed to the operator's terminal. The web UI never persists it.
- Verse agents authenticate to the server only with their per-turn `Authorization: Bearer` token, on the MCP route. This route refuses any `Authorization` header outright.
- The phone gateway forwards mutations server-side, with no `Origin`, and only for paths on its allowlist (`remote-gateway-policy.ts`). This path is on neither.

Remaining risk, not created by this change: a local process running as Mason can still edit `~/.ashlr/comms.toml` directly, as it always could.

## Commands run

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/comms-confirm.test.ts` | 9/9 pass |
| `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/comms-confirm-route.test.ts` | 7/7 pass |
| `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run --config vitest.config.web.ts src/web-ui/routes/verse/comms-confirm/CommsConfirmCard.test.tsx` | 4/4 pass |
| Same web config: NeedsYouDrawer tests, `subset-glyphs`, `control-density`, `style-scan-310`, `VerseApp.first-paint` | 168/169 pass |

The one web failure is pre-existing and unrelated: `style-scan-310` flags px font fallbacks in `routes/verse/growth/GrowthCharts.module.css`, a file this change does not touch.

**ESLint was not run.** It crashes on start in this worktree because `node_modules/eslint/lib` is missing ("Cannot find module '../lib/cli'"), so the install is broken. I did not reinstall dependencies.

**Typecheck:** `npx --no-install tsgo` is not installed (npm 404), so I ran the fallback `npx --no-install tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` once in the foreground: exit 0. A first `tsc` attempt was killed at a 20-minute tool timeout before it printed anything; the second run completed.

**Rebase check:** after `git fetch origin master` (now a4e6cb65dd), the tracked diff applies cleanly to origin/master (`git apply --cached --check` against a temporary index), and none of the touched or new paths changed upstream.

## Net LOC

- Source: +413 lines (`comms-confirm.ts` 167, route 97, card 91 + CSS 49, wiring 9).
- Tests: +267 lines.
- Docs: +3 lines.

Source is slightly over the ~400 target, mostly because of the CSS.
</details>

title: bridge: RQ-SEC-REALHOME-1
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-SEC-REALHOME-1` (pool: claude), single commit on base `07617f688`.

**Tests:** no test command

**Tier-1 (CODEOWNERS) paths, async post-merge review:** .github/CODEOWNERS src/core/fleet/tick-hooks-live.ts src/core/sandbox/execution-leases.ts src/core/sandbox/mutation-fence.ts src/core/sandbox/policy.ts test/fixtures/authority/tier1-closure.json test/h4.sandbox-enrollment-kill.test.ts test/helpers/h1-fixture.ts test/setup/home.ts test/setup/real-home-child.cjs

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# RQ-SEC-REALHOME-1: authority reads from the account home, not HOME

G1 review: Security (-sec), RQ-SEC-REALHOME-1. Security Hardening Engineer authored
the finding and is the G1 reviewer.

## Summary

Authority paths for KILL, the outward mutation fence, execution leases, comms
pause, the send gate, owner and team identity, standing approvals and the
iMessage and email outbox recipients were all built from `os.homedir()`, which
follows `$HOME`. A child started with a relocated HOME saw KILL inactive, comms
unpaused, and accepted forged recipients. This change:

- (a) Adds `realHome()` (`src/core/util/real-home.ts`): `os.userInfo().homedir`,
  must be absolute, else throws (callers fail closed). There is no environment
  override (HOME, USERPROFILE, ASHLR_HOME, ASHLR_RUNS_DIR or any new variable).
  win32 falls back to `os.homedir()`; this is a documented follow-up in
  docs/COMMS-AGENT.md, since USERPROFILE carries the same risk. When HOME
  differs from the account home, the process logs one line, "HOME differs from
  account home; authority read from account home", with no paths. Every
  resolver listed in F1 and F2 now uses it. The three duplicated
  `canonicalHome()` copies (policy, mutation-fence, execution-leases) are
  deleted in favor of `canonicalRealHome()`.
- (b) Adds `outsideSendBlock()` (`src/core/comms/transport-gate.ts`), which
  checks KILL and then comms pause, both from the account home, and fails
  closed: any read error counts as blocked. It is called at the top of
  `sendIMessage`, `sendIMessageOutbox`, `sendTelegramMessage`, `sendEmailOutbox`
  and `macMailTransport`. `localWriteGate()` now delegates to it. The cli/comms
  cycle send goes through `sendEmailOutbox`, so it is covered. A refused send
  spawns nothing and makes no request. Owner-only alerts are blocked during
  KILL too; the decision on whether an owner alert may bypass KILL is pending
  with Mason and is recorded in docs/COMMS-AGENT.md.
- (c) Adds `osascript`, `osacompile`, `open`, `shortcuts` and `automator` to the
  engineer bash deny-list, matching the autonomous lane profile
  (`sandbox/confine.ts`). `open`, `shortcuts` and `automator` match only in
  command position (line start, after `; & | ( $(` or backtick, after
  `xargs`/`env`/`exec`/... or `sh -c`, with optional `VAR=x` prefixes and path
  qualification), so arguments like `cat open.txt` still pass.

### Findings discovered while implementing (please review)

1. **`phm demo` would have written the real `~/.ashlr`.** `src/cli/demo-sandbox.ts`
   isolated itself by setting `process.env.HOME` in-process, then enrolled a
   throwaway repo and ran a tick. With authority on the account home, that
   enrollment and its audit would have hit the operator's real enrollment.json.
   Fix: the demo now (1) refuses to start if the account-home KILL is on, then
   (2) calls `enterIsolatedAuthorityHome(tmpHome)`, an in-process function
   (no env, so no child can select it) that scopes authority to the throwaway
   home until `dispose()`. (3) While a scope is active, `outsideSendBlock()`
   blocks every outside send. This is the only production HOME relocator in
   src/. Security: please confirm this narrow scope is acceptable, or say if
   you prefer the demo be refused outright.
2. **Pause acknowledgments would have been silenced.** The Telegram `pause`
   command (`comms/dispatch.ts`) and the iMessage pause-fleet action
   (`comms/handlers.ts`) set the pause and then sent the owner an ack, which
   the new gate refuses. Both now send the ack first, then set the pause in a
   `finally`, so a failed ack can never skip the pause.
3. **Extra KILL readers swapped for consistency.** These were not listed but
   read `~/.ashlr/KILL` through `homedir()`: `integrations/pulse-exporter.ts`,
   `integrations/pulse-sync.ts` (both export outward) and
   `fleet/tick-hooks-live.ts` (pace advice). `release/train.ts` was left
   untouched as instructed.
4. **Behavior change for relocated-HOME children (intended).** The self-swap
   rehearsal daemon (`daemon/self-swap-runtime.ts`), the autonomous sandbox env
   and the engineer bash scratch HOME now see the real KILL, enrollment, leases
   and config.json. That is the point of the fix, but a rehearsal daemon now
   reads, and could write, real enrollment and config state. Security may want
   to look at self-swap specifically.
5. **No account home means fail closed.** If `os.userInfo()` throws (a uid with
   no passwd entry, e.g. some containers), authority resolvers fail closed:
   KILL counts as on, comms counts as paused, and `config.ts` throws at import
   (CONFIG_DIR). The CLI is unusable in such a container by design.

### Test-harness migration (hermeticity)

- `test/setup/home.ts` sets the seam to `{kind:'homedir'}` for every suite, so
  in-process authority follows the guarded relocated HOME (or a suite's own
  `node:os` mock), exactly as before. It writes the global the module reads
  rather than importing it, so test-file `vi.mock('node:os')` still applies.
- Node children: `test/setup/real-home-child.cjs` is added to `NODE_OPTIONS`
  through `--require`. It applies the same seam in tsx/node children, honored
  only when `VITEST` is set. It uses `--require` because any `--import` forces
  the ESM loader on the child's main entry, which broke extensionless engine
  fixtures (`grok-0.2.118-macos-aarch64`). It is never shipped (test/ is not in
  package `files`).
- Children spawned with a scrubbed env get no seam and resolve the real account
  home. While running the suites I instrumented `realHome()` to log every
  divergence to a file. The only real-home child found was
  `test/config-set-help-exit.test.ts` (read-only `--help`); it now passes
  `VITEST` and `NODE_OPTIONS` through. Caveat: the file log covered batches
  ac to af and the reruns; batches aa and ab were covered only by stderr.
  The instrumentation is removed.
- `test/helpers/h1-fixture.ts` pins the seam to its tmp home explicitly and
  restores it in `cleanup()`. Its sanity guard also checks `realHome()`.
- `test/h4.sandbox-enrollment-kill.test.ts` 3.11 moves the seam along with HOME
  for its alternate-root case.
- The seam: `__setRealHomeForTests(path | 'homedir' | null)` throws unless
  `VITEST` is set and returns the previous value. `realHome()` ignores any
  leftover override when `VITEST` is unset (tested).

## Resolvers swapped to realHome() (file:line, current tree)

- KILL / enrollment (ashlrDir): src/core/sandbox/policy.ts:262 (also 426, 551, 1771, 2026, 2121)
- Outward fence: src/core/sandbox/mutation-fence.ts:61, 138
- Execution lease dir: src/core/sandbox/execution-leases.ts:118
- Comms pause: src/core/comms/pause.ts:24, 74
- Send policy (comms.toml, agent-network.toml): src/core/agents/send-gate.ts:20 (unreadable home grants nothing)
- Standing approvals path and walk anchor: src/core/comms-agent/store.ts:76, 304; runs-root fallback 68
- CONFIG_DIR / resolveConfigDir (comms.imessageHandle, telegram chatId and token): src/core/config.ts:42, 59
- Teammates registry: src/core/comms/imessage-outbox.ts:19
- Email allowlist runsDir defaults: src/cli/fleet-email-outbox.ts:77, 83, 117; src/cli/comms.ts:363, 403, 772
- Goal conductor permit operator: src/core/daemon/goal-conductor-permit-operator.ts:209, 553, 898
- iMessage state dir fallback: src/core/integrations/imessage.ts:360
- Extra KILL readers: src/core/integrations/pulse-exporter.ts:202, src/core/integrations/pulse-sync.ts:244, src/core/fleet/tick-hooks-live.ts:715
- Demo scope: src/cli/demo-sandbox.ts:151

Transport gate call sites: src/core/integrations/imessage.ts:110,
src/core/comms/imessage-outbox.ts:37, src/core/integrations/telegram.ts:714,
src/core/comms/email-outbox.ts:235 (sendEmailOutbox), 364 (macMailTransport),
src/core/agents/send-gate.ts:13 (localWriteGate).

## Files

New: src/core/util/real-home.ts, src/core/comms/transport-gate.ts,
test/real-home-authority.test.ts, test/setup/real-home-child.cjs.
Modified (src): sandbox/policy.ts, sandbox/mutation-fence.ts,
sandbox/execution-leases.ts, comms/pause.ts, comms/imessage-outbox.ts,
comms/email-outbox.ts, comms/dispatch.ts, comms/handlers.ts, agents/send-gate.ts,
comms-agent/store.ts, config.ts, integrations/imessage.ts,
integrations/telegram.ts, integrations/pulse-exporter.ts,
integrations/pulse-sync.ts, fleet/tick-hooks-live.ts,
daemon/goal-conductor-permit-operator.ts, mcp-native-engineer.ts,
cli/comms.ts, cli/fleet-email-outbox.ts, cli/demo.ts, cli/demo-sandbox.ts.
Modified (tests): test/setup/home.ts, test/helpers/h1-fixture.ts,
test/m42.engineer-tools.test.ts, test/h4.sandbox-enrollment-kill.test.ts,
test/config-set-help-exit.test.ts.
Generated by `npm run authority:regen`: .github/CODEOWNERS (one line adding
/test/real-home-authority.test.ts) and test/fixtures/authority/tier1-closure.json
(adds real-home.ts and transport-gate.ts to the Tier-1 closure).
Docs: CONTRACT.md (config.ts note, real-home.ts section),
docs/COMMS-AGENT.md (transport gate, pending owner-alert decision, account home, win32 follow-up).

Net LOC: about +640 (tracked +260/-107, plus about 480 new lines in four new files).

## Commands and results

All runs use the per-worker temp HOME from test/setup/home.ts. No real ~/.ashlr
was created or touched. The machine was heavily loaded (about 30 concurrent
lanes), so many 5 s test timeouts are environmental. Every failure was
compared against an unmodified copy of HEAD (`git archive HEAD`, same
node_modules) running the same files.

- `npx vitest run test/real-home-authority.test.ts`: 28/28 pass (KILL, pause,
  send policy, approvals, config.json, email allowlist, lease census, ASHLR_HOME
  and ASHLR_RUNS_DIR regression, seam, divergence log, transport gates with
  KILL and pause and fail-closed, demo scope).
- `test/m42.engineer-tools.test.ts`: pass, including 9 new deny-list cases.

  send-gate, comms*, comms-agent*, imessage*, telegram*, email-outbox*,

  6 JSON batches:
  - aa: 530 pass / 7 fail. Fixed: config-set-help-exit (2). Rest also fail on
    baseline or are load timeouts.
  - ab: 584 pass / 16 fail. Fixed: engines-stream-family preload regression,
    h4 3.11. Remaining (execution-leases foreign owner, h4 1.6, loop-stall,
    no-diff-stall group-exit) also fail on baseline: process probes and `ps`
    are not permitted in this sandbox.
  - ac: 800 pass / 29 fail. Fixed: h8.demo (finding 1). Remaining:
    int4-confine (`sandbox-exec` not permitted), m169 and m429 (fail on

  - ad: 1079 pass / 13 fail (rerun after a SIGTERM). Compared on both trees

    on baseline. m426 passes alone on both trees.
  - af: 738 pass / 2 fail. throughput-310b fails the same on baseline.
- Targeted comparison of 9 files (outcome-daemon-loop, mirror-git-bounded,

  baseline 119 pass / 44 fail, change 116 pass / 47 fail. All three extra

- `m461.demo-activation-refusal`: 4/4 pass alone (3.4 to 3.7 s vs baseline 3.7 to 4.2 s).

body:

**Tier-1 (CODEOWNERS) paths, async post-merge review:** .github/CODEOWNERS src/core/vision/leader-seat.ts test/fixtures/authority/tier1-closure.json

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES: RQ-ROUTER-GATEWAY

## Summary

This change adds a router gateway: one routed model call for any agent, built on `routeSeat`. There is one code path, one versioned config, and three ways in.

- **Core** (`src/core/router-gateway/`)
  - `config.ts`: the versioned config `~/.ashlr/router/gateway.json` (`version: 1`). It sets the lanes `auto` may use, model aliases, the port, `maxAttempts`, `timeoutMs` and `maxConcurrent`.
    - Unknown keys are refused. There is no host key and no credential key.
    - `phm router config --init` writes the defaults (mode 0600) and never overwrites an existing file.
  - `complete.ts`: `routedComplete`, `planRoutedCompletion` and `listRouterModels`, the single path.
    - `auto` ranks the configured lanes through `routeSeat`.
    - `<lane>:<model>` pins one lane but passes the same admission: standing grant for the `producer` role, engine in the grant, local-only mode, the Codex subscription-only boundary, budget clamp, reserves, headroom and context fit.
    - A failed seat falls through to the next ranked seat, up to `maxAttempts`.
    - Native calls recheck admission throughout the call.
    - The kill switch stops every call. Routing previews still work.
    - Local models must be on 127.0.0.1; a remote Ollama is ruled out.
    - Decisions go to the shadow log with source `gateway` (that source already existed).
  - `deps.ts`: production wiring.
    - It reuses the Leader's seat discovery, capacity, budget and grant reads.
    - Native seats run through `nativeRoleCompletion` as role `worker`, so provider auth stays in each lane CLI and keychain. Local models run through Ollama (free text) or the bound llama-server.
  - `server.ts`: the loopback OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
    - It binds `127.0.0.1` only, hardcoded, and asserts the bound address after listen.
    - Requests with a non-loopback `Host` or `Origin` get 403.
    - It requires a bearer token from a 0600 file `~/.ashlr/router/token`, compared in constant time, and never printed.
    - Routes: `GET /v1/models`, `POST /v1/chat/completions` (`stream: true` sends one SSE chunk, then `[DONE]`), `GET /healthz`.
    - Tools, images and `n≠1` get 400. The body is capped at 2 MiB and requests past the concurrency limit get 429.
- **CLI** (`src/cli/router-gateway.ts`, thin)
  - `phm router serve|models|pick|config [--json]`.
  - `phm run --model auto|<lane:model> "<prompt>" [--system] [--task] [--difficulty] [--json]` is one routed completion.
    - Plain Ollama tags such as `--model qwen3:8b` keep their old goal-run meaning.
    - Only `auto` or a lane starting with `claude`, `codex`, `grok` or `local` routes.
- **MCP**: `phm_router_plan` (read) returns the same `router.plan.v1` routing plan and calls no model. This is deliberately narrower than the spec; see the decision below.
- **Docs and examples**
  - `docs/ROUTER-GATEWAY.md` (plain English, copy-paste examples, output shapes, exit codes).
  - `examples/router-gateway/agent.mjs`: a sample agent call with no dependencies. It refuses a non-loopback URL and never prints the token.
  - Entries in `llms.txt`, `docs/llms.txt`, AGENTS.md ("Router gateway") and `docs/README.md`; a row in `docs/MCP-TOOLS.md`; help and completion entries; regenerated `docs/cli.md`, `docs/CLI-REFERENCE.md` and `docs/CODEMAP.md`.
- **Small change to existing code**: `ollamaLeaderTransport` gains an optional `json?: boolean`. The default is unchanged (JSON-constrained output); the gateway passes `false` for free text.

## Decisions and deviations, for review

1. **The MCP tool is read-only (`phm_router_plan`), not a completion tool.**
   - `CONTRACT-M31` limits native MCP tools to the classes `read`, `append` and `proposal`. Invariant 3 says no native tool may reach a cloud model, and `test/m31.native-tools.test.ts` enforces the classes.
   - A completion tool that can route to Claude, Codex or Grok would break that contract, so the MCP surface previews the same routing step instead. Completions go through `phm run --model` or the loopback endpoint.
   - If you want an MCP completion tool, that is a contract change for you to decide.
2. **Dependency gate.**
   - RQ-METER-PACE-1 landed as #4209 ("Pace lanes so included usage meets each reset").
   - I could not find RQ-ROUTE-OPTIMAL on master, and `gh` is blocked in this sandbox (it cannot read `~/.config/gh`).
   - The gateway only calls `routeSeat`, `rankEligibleCapacities` is not used, and it does not depend on how ranking works inside. A later ROUTE-OPTIMAL change to scoring flows through without edits here. Please confirm the gate before merging.
3. **Security pin and owner review needed.**
   - `mcp-native.ts` is in the Tier-1 import closure, so the five `src/core/router-gateway/*.ts` files joined it.
   - I regenerated with `npm run authority:regen`. That updated `test/fixtures/authority/tier1-closure.json` and added `/test/router-gateway.test.ts @masonwyatt23` to `.github/CODEOWNERS`.
   - `src/core/vision/leader-seat.ts` is code-owned. The edit there is the two-line, additive `json` option.
   - No workflow permissions, secrets refs, triggers or third-party actions changed.
4. **"dispatchd lanes through it".**
   - Every dispatchd lane that has a seat can be addressed as `<seat-id>:<model>`, for example `codex-personal:gpt-5.5` or `grok:grok-4.6`, and is ranked by `auto`. Devin cloud sessions keep their own lane, the same rule as the router.
   - dispatchd's own agent spawns (Claude Code or Codex sessions working in worktrees) are agent CLIs, not chat completions. They are not rerouted through the endpoint in this change.
   - The sample agent call is `examples/router-gateway/agent.mjs`, exercised end to end in `test/router-gateway.test.ts`: script → HTTP → routeSeat → transport.
5. Gateway calls are always `autonomous: true`, so the owner's reserves apply because the callers are agents. The grant role is `producer`, matching `nativeRoleCompletion` for the `worker` role.
6. Seat discovery runs on every request. That keeps admission fresh, at the cost of about a second per call. A short cache can come later if it matters.
7. Two small fixes to existing drift in files I touched:
   - Added `claim` to `TOP_LEVEL_COMMANDS`; `cli-registry-drift` was red on master.
   - Classified `phantom_spend_budget` in `test/mcp-output-efficiency.test.ts` on its own measured cap (236 bytes measured, 260 allowed), next to `phm_router_plan` (474 measured, 500 allowed). It was red on master.
   - No existing cap was raised.

## Commands run

- `npm run typecheck:fast` failed because `tsgo` is not installed (npm 404). `node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` passed (exit 0).
- `node scripts/verify-changed.mjs`:
  - First run: authority drift. I fixed it with `npm run authority:regen`.
  - Second run: file selection, authority drift, realio lane lint and verse sync-I/O lint all PASS.
  - The second run's `tsc --noEmit` step reported FAIL with no diagnostics. The direct tsc run above passed, so it was probably the slot or timeout under machine load.
  - ESLint was skipped because `node_modules/eslint` is absent; Merge Gate lints on CI.
- `npm run check:docs`: 0 errors.
- `npm run docs:sync`: regenerated the CLI docs, CODEMAP and the `docs/llms.txt` index.
  - I reverted its unrelated release version-pin bumps (`docs/QUICKSTART.md`, `examples/quickstart.md`, `site/llms-full.txt`) to stay out of the release train.
- `npm run authority:regen`, run twice; the second run showed no changes.
- Tests, with `HOME=$(mktemp -d)` and `--testTimeout=60000`:
  - `test/router-gateway.test.ts`: 18 passed.
  - The full affected set (router-gateway, m31.contract-lock, m42.engineer-tools, doc-facts, cli-registry-drift, leader-seat-310b, leader-seat-transports-310b, m31.native-tools, m129.agent-surface, m31.safety, mcp-output-efficiency, authority-tier1-closure-310b, authority-codeowners-310b, docs-mcp-tools, docs-sync): **252 passed, 10 failed**. All 10 also fail on master:
    - 9 in `docs-mcp-tools`: the test can't find the `desktop_*` names written out in `src/core/mcp-native.ts` on master, because they come from the `desktopOperatorTools` spread.
    - 1 in `docs-sync`: the 3.30.28 version-pin drift, which the release train owns.
  - At the default 5 s timeout, some m31 tests timed out under machine load. They pass with a longer timeout.
- Manual smoke test with a scratch HOME (`node --import tsx src/cli/index.ts …`):
  - `router config --init --json`, `router models --json` and `router pick --model auto --json` (exit 1, no seats) ran as expected; `pick --model nope` exited 2.
  - `run --model auto "hello" --json` returned `router.completion.v1` with no-route, exit 1.
  - `router serve --port 18799 --json`:
    - `lsof` showed it listening on `127.0.0.1` only, with the token file at mode 0600.
    - `/healthz` returned 200. A request with no token got 401, and `Host: evil.example` got 403.
    - `/v1/models` returned 200, chat returned 503 no-route, and the sample agent exited 1 with the reason.

  - No real model was called. This machine's Ollama has no models, and native seats need host accounts that a scratch HOME does not have.

## Net LOC

`report-2000.md` from recorded state only: the world model snapshot
(`phm world --json` read path), the trailing 12 h of
`metrics/jobs.jsonl` (growth), leader intents (operator directives,
self-directives, open goals, pending proposals, queue next-up) and a bounded
`gh run list` read for Actions run ids/URLs. PR URLs recorded as
published/merged in the ledger are the PR evidence. Every source degrades
independently — a missing snapshot, unreadable ledger, absent `gh` or partial
intents store produces an explicit `unavailable`/`incomplete` line, never a
zero. All rendered text passes through `scrubSecrets`; writes are atomic,
0600, under the existing private-file conventions.

Scheduling is LaunchAgent-free inside `contrib/mac/dispatchd.py`: once a
slot's build time passes in America/New_York (07:25 → `report-0730.md`,
19:55 → `report-2000.md`) a tick spawns `bin/report-export.sh` until the
day's file exists. The report's own `day=YYYY-MM-DD` marker is the
idempotence; `.report-<slot>.tries` bounds retries at 3 launches per slot per
day; `export/REPORTS_OFF` is the kill switch; `REPORTS_TEST` +

`managed` file in `fleet/manifest.json` (installs via `fleet/sync.py`), and
the dispatchd schedule is a pinned-file change — it goes live only after
Security re-pins and installs via `contrib/mac/install.sh`. No pinned file
was overwritten; no live `~/.ashlr-runs/bin` install was run; nothing was
committed, pushed, tagged or published.

title: bridge: RQ-CONNECTOR-PROFILE-2
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-CONNECTOR-PROFILE-2` (pool: claude), single commit on base `74e22d6f1`.

**Tests:** no test command

**Tier-1 (CODEOWNERS) paths, async post-merge review:** test/config/realio-lane-membership.mjs

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# RQ-CONNECTOR-PROFILE-2: credential injection at launch

Dependency gate: RQ-CONNECTOR-PROFILE-1 merged as b567a71418 (#3290).
**SECURITY GATE: do not merge without a Security pin (Security Hardening Engineer 606e84d2).**
Nothing is committed or pushed.

## Design

Phantom Secrets has no non-TTY plaintext path by design (`phantom reveal` needs a
trusted terminal). Its sanctioned launch path is `phantom exec`. That command
resolves vault entries for the project in its working directory, keeps real
values inside a loopback proxy, and hands its child only session tokens
(`phm_` + 64 hex). Phantom never receives or holds a credential value.

```
phm connectors exec <id> --tool T --lane L [--project DIR] -- <command> [args]
  credentials = []  -> <command> <profile args> <args>   (PHANTOM_* internals scrubbed)
  credentials != [] -> phantom --quiet exec -- phm connectors exec-session <id> --tool T --lane L -- <command> ...
                         -> exec-session re-reads + re-validates the profile,
                            sets binding = session token phantom issued for the vault name,
                            drops every other session token (least privilege),
                            starts <command> <profile args> <args>
```

Controls:
- Only `cli` and `mcp-stdio` kinds start a process.
- The tool and lane must both be explicitly listed on the connector. Empty lists deny.
- `cmd[0]` must equal the profile `command` exactly, so a connector's credentials
  never reach another program.
- Extra args pass the existing credential-argument and secret-shape refusal.
- `exec-session` refuses to run outside `phantom exec` (it requires
  `PHANTOM_PROXY_TOKEN`). It fails closed when a referenced name is not listed in
  `PHANTOM_SESSION_KEYS` or is not a session-token shape, so an ambient
  plaintext value is never forwarded. It only remaps tokens already in its env.
- On success, exec writes nothing to stdout (the MCP stdio stream stays clean).
  It propagates the child exit status (128+signal) and forwards SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP.
- Spawn errors use a static message because the raw error would echo a path.
- `--project` must be absolute and outside any `.codex` path.

`phm connectors config --client claude|cursor|codex --lane L [--project DIR] [--json]`
prints the client MCP snippet (JSON `mcpServers` / Codex TOML `mcp_servers`).
Stdio servers become `phm connectors exec ...` entries with no env and no headers.
Credential-free HTTP endpoints become `url` entries. HTTP connectors that carry
credentials are skipped and reported (exit 1). Every snippet goes through
`assertMetadata` before it is printed. The command writes no files, so it never
touches `~/.codex`.

## Not done / follow-ups (report)
- **HTTP header injection** for `mcp-http` connectors is not provided. These
  connectors are skipped with a reason. They would need a phantom proxy route or
  a stdio bridge.
- **Name constraint**: credential `name` must be a key that Phantom Secrets
  protects in the project's managed dotenv (env-var shaped, e.g. `GITHUB_ACCESS`),
  because `phantom exec` keys its session tokens by dotenv key. Bindings may differ.
- **Custody**: `phantom exec` takes custody from its cwd. Clients that launch MCP
  servers from arbitrary directories need `--project` in the generated entry.
- **Same-user visibility**: session tokens sit in the child environment, which the
  same user can see with `ps eww`. These are phantom session tokens, valid only
  through that session's loopback proxy, and never real values.
- `phm connectors run` (scope + Locus grant) and registry `connector-call` stay
  denied. They are unchanged and remain a separate Security line.
- `config` prints only and does not write client files. Writing them through
  `phm wire` is a possible follow-up.
- ESLint could not run: `node_modules/eslint/lib/cli.js` is missing in both this
  worktree and the main checkout. Merge Gate lints on CI.

## Commands run (HOME set to a fresh mktemp dir each time)
- `npx vitest run test/connector-exec.test.ts test/connector-profile.test.ts`: 40/40 pass
- `npx vitest run test/doc-facts.test.ts test/connectors-run.test.ts test/tool-mesh.test.ts test/tool-registry.test.ts test/connector-manager.test.ts test/cli-help-safety-core.test.ts test/cli-help-exit.test.ts`:
  76/77 on first run. The one failure was the tool-mesh assertion pinned to the old
  "denied" route, which this change intentionally replaces. It now asserts the
  exec route, and `test/tool-mesh.test.ts` passes 1/1.
- `npm run check:docs`: 0 errors
- `node scripts/docs-sync.mjs`: regenerated docs/cli.md and docs/CLI-REFERENCE.md.
  Unrelated pre-existing drift (version bumps, codemap, other llms lines) was reverted to keep scope.
- `node scripts/verify-changed.mjs`: authority drift PASS, realio lane lint PASS,
  verse lint PASS. ESLint SKIP (missing install). tsc timed out at 900s under heavy machine load.
- Scoped `tsc` (repo tsconfig, files: exec.ts, client-config.ts, cli/connectors.ts, mesh.ts, connector-exec test + fixture and their import graph): exit 0, 0 diagnostics.

Secret-shape evidence: tests run `.github/tests/secret-shape/scrub.pl --check` over
every generated client config (claude, cursor, codex) and over the JSON result
(exit 0). The end-to-end test records the argv of the fake phantom and the shim
and asserts it contains no token.

Note: the sandbox in this environment refuses to exec any file named `phantom`,
so the test fake is named `fake-phantom` and is passed in through `phantomBin`.

# RQ-GROK-AS-LANE-1: Grok as a world-model resource

Grok Ultra is now a resource with capacity, a reset time and a manual reading. At zero capacity the Grok lane is zero until the reset; no other lane is touched.

title: bridge: RQ-SWE5-LOOP-BENCH
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-SWE5-LOOP-BENCH` (pool: devin), single commit on base `3d2173645`.

**Tests:** no test command

**Sensitive paths (needs Security OK):** contrib/mac/publish.sh 

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# RQ-SWE5-LOOP-BENCH — outer-loop efficiency benchmark

Measured the deterministic Mac loop's own speed and optimized the hottest paths.
Goal: the loop should be as fast as the agents it launches.

## Research digest

`~/.ashlr-runs/coordination/phantom-productive-20261105/RESEARCH-DIGEST.md` could
not be read: macOS denies this shell's processes access under `~/.ashlr-runs`
(`Operation not permitted` on stat/cat — TCC). The task prompt and repository
sources were self-contained, so work proceeded without it.

## Benchmark harness

New `contrib/mac/bench_loop.py` builds a synthetic `~/.ashlr-runs` (stubbed
`ps`/`ashlr`/`memory_pressure`/`sysctl`, real `~/.ashlr-runs/bin/*` shims, real
git fixture repos, a pre-filled shared Cargo target) and times:

- `tick`: one full `dispatchd.py` run under an isolated HOME
- `launch_preflight` / `launch_total`: `disk.launch()` up to / through `supervised()`
- `publish`: `disk.finish()` (quarantine → worktree remove → deferred trim)
- `reap`: `disk.reap_pending()` over 4 cached repo targets (~6000 files)
- `pick`: `restock.py --dry-run` over a 300-line router queue
- `--profile`: cProfile of a tick

Fixture (identical before/after): `jobs_rows=40000, ready=60, base_files=45,
queue_lines=300, cache_files=3000`, 5 runs per stage, medians reported.
Baseline measured against HEAD copies of the touched files extracted to
`/tmp/loop-bench-base/` and passed via `--dispatchd/--restock/--disk`.

## Results (median ms, same fixture)

| stage            | before  | after   | delta     |
|------------------|---------|---------|-----------|
| tick             | 2133.08 | 1850.61 | **−13.2%**|
| launch_preflight | 277.22  | 273.74  | −1.3%     |
| launch_total     | 1360.42 | 1359.72 | −0.1%     |
| publish          | 580.97  | 592.16  | +1.9% (noise) |
| reap             | 468.40  | 876.78  | see note  |
| pick             | 1639.43 | 1321.54 | **−19.4%**|

`reap`: the two-run gap is measurement noise — the stage is dominated by `du`
filesystem scans. An interleaved re-measure (9 alternating runs) gives
before=750 ms, after=716 ms — flat, with one fewer subprocess per snapshot.

Fixture caveat: stubbed probes return in ~0.9 s; on the real host the six
probes ran *sequentially* for ~1.5–1.8 s/tick (baseline profile: ~1.79 s in
`subprocess`/`select.poll`). They now overlap, so the real-tick gain should be
larger than the fixture's 13%.

## Optimizations

### `contrib/mac/dispatchd.py`
- **Parallel probes**: `_autopilot`, `mem`, `capture_process_snapshot`,
  `_daemon_tick_age`, `api_pace`, claude-api `report` run on a 6-worker
  `ThreadPoolExecutor`, submitted once and collected at their original decision
  points. Tick critical path becomes `max(probes)` ≈ mem (~0.9 s) instead of
  their serial sum (~1.8 s in the baseline profile).
- **Single ledger parse**: `jobs.jsonl` was parsed 3×/tick (attempts scan,
  `_devin_spike`, status rollup) plus once more for batch throughput — ~120k
  `json.loads` per tick at this fixture size. Now parsed once into `JOBS_RAW`
  and projected once into `JOBS` via new `batcher.parse_rows`/`project_rows`;
  `metric()` mirrors post-parse writes so later phases see this tick's own rows
  exactly as a re-read would (`_JOBS_LIVE` gate prevents double-counting
  pre-parse `metric()` calls, e.g. `ab_unhold()`).
- **Bounded events tail**: status rollup used `rd(EV)` (whole growing log);
  now `logtail(EV, 65536)`.
- **Parallel `_ph_check`**: the seven `gh api` queued-run counts run on a
  `ThreadPoolExecutor`; any failure still abandons the check unwritten
  (fail-closed preserved).
- **`rd()` mtime/size cache**: queue metadata (`.line`, `.base`, `.publish`,
  prompts, `ready.tsv`, `slots.json`) is re-read many times per tick. Cache
  keyed on `(st_mtime_ns, st_size)`; a mid-tick rewrite invalidates exactly as
  a fresh read. Misses are never cached.

### `contrib/mac/batcher.py`
- `read_rows` split into `parse_rows` (decode), `project_row`, `project_rows`
  so dispatchd pays parse+project once. `read_rows` remains as the composed
  wrapper — no other caller changed.

### `contrib/mac/restock.py`
- `router-queue.md` is read once (`RQ_TXT`) instead of once per READY line
  inside the pick loop's `sub of <job>` grep.

### `scripts/bridge/disk.py`
- `identity()`: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel --path-format=absolute
  --git-common-dir --absolute-git-dir` in one call (3→1 subprocess); still
  validates exactly 3 lines and enforces the linked-worktree/locked checks.
- `du_many()`: one `du -sk` for all snapshot roots; missing→0, failed→None
  (du omits failed roots from stdout — verified), preserving the
  "unknown is not zero" contract.
- `launch()`: the pre-launch `du` is reused by `check_budget` instead of being
  re-measured; after `clean_cache` the known-empty target skips re-measure.
- `supervised()`: the per-second full-`du` budget probe now runs at a 4 s
  cadence; the cheap `disk_usage` floor check still runs every interval.
- `finish()`: dropped the redundant post-quarantine `verify_clean` —
  `publication()` already ran it, only untracked files move in between (which
  `verify_clean` never inspects), and `git worktree remove` refuses a dirty
  tree. The remaining `--others` check is the true invariant.

### `contrib/mac/publish.sh`
- `git add -N` and `git show $BASE:<CODEOWNERS>` batched (3 spawns → 1 each).
- The upstream `defaultBranchRef` lookup and both `scrub.pl --check` runs now
  execute concurrently while the push is in flight; DEF result is collected
  and validated after push (`RESULT ABORT default-branch` replaces the
  previous silent-empty path that failed later at `gh pr create`).

## Commands run

- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) python3 contrib/mac/bench_loop.py` (after; `--dispatchd/--restock/--disk` pointed at `/tmp/loop-bench-base` for baseline)
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) python3 contrib/mac/bench_loop.py --runs 1 --profile --profile-top 14`
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) python3 -m unittest discover -s contrib/mac/tests -p 'test_<f>.py'` for every contrib/mac suite
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/bridge -p 'test_disk.py'`
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) node scripts/verify-changed.mjs`
- `bash -n contrib/mac/publish.sh`; `python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(...)"` on each touched .py

## Tests

Pass/fail: **365 passed, 0 failed** in touched suites; suite-wide two
pre-existing environmental errors unrelated to this diff:

- `test_integrated_merge.test_hung_grandchild_pipe_has_bounded_own_group_cleanup`
  — sandbox denies `/bin/ps` (TCC `Operation not permitted`).
- `test_native_pressure_boundary` — requires the host fixture packet
  `wt/reference/ACTUAL-READONLY-launch.sh`, absent in this worktree.

New coverage:
- `test_batcher.py`: `parse_rows` decodes only / skips bad lines / absent file;
  `project_row` identity for dispatcher rows; projection boundary.
- `test_disk.py`: `du_many` runs exactly one subprocess and keeps
  unreadable≠zero; `identity` issues exactly one `rev-parse`.
- `test_disk.test_unknown_du_size_is_not_treated_as_zero` updated to patch the
  new `du_many` boundary — assertion semantics unchanged (unknown ⇒ Refused ⇒
  logged `du_bytes` field stays `None`).

Per-suite counts: test_disk 41, test_batcher 18, test_dispatchd 65,
test_batching 5, test_restock 42, test_ready_lock 3, test_restock_append_race 2,
test_concurrency ~OK, test_host_machine_sample 1, test_install_gate 10,
test_install 8, test_loadgate 43, test_local_job 4, test_metrics_outcomes 11,
test_precheck_backoff 2, test_process_snapshot 8, test_publish_dependency_links
39, test_release_autorun 35, test_route_hysteresis OK, test_sb17_sandbox 8,
test_staged_drain 15, test_integrated_merge 72+1env-error,
test_native_pressure_boundary env-error.

`node scripts/verify-changed.mjs`: PASS (file selection, `tsc --noEmit`, lane
lints; eslint skipped — `node_modules/eslint` absent, Merge Gate lints on CI).

## Net LOC

+252 / −76 = **+176** on tracked files, plus new `bench_loop.py` (+367,
untracked harness). All changes are uncommitted in the worktree.

## Notes / limits

- Behavior preserved: probes, holds, gates, ledger projections and all
  security checks (fork-guard, scrub gates, verify_clean, fail-closed publish)
  unchanged — only scheduling and read deduplication differ.
- `dispatchd.py`, `restock.py`, `publish.sh` are pinned live-host files; a
  Security re-pin is required before `contrib/mac/install.sh` install.
</details>

body:

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE5-ACTION-CLASSES

## Summary

Implemented the unified action-class autonomy registry (research digest item 7
as stated in the job brief). One canonical registry —
`src/core/authority/action-classes.ts` — enumerates the eight action classes
(`read`, `write-worktree`, `publish`, `merge`, `close`, `release`,
`external-comms`, `secrets-touch`), each with an explicit gate policy
(`open`, `confined-launch`, `publish-pipeline`, `merge-queue`,
`release-channel`, `channel-approval`, `operator`, `forbidden`), a blast radius
(`none` … `credentials`, plus `unknown` sorting widest), and reversibility
metadata (`free`, `revertible`, `costly`, `irreversible`).

The registry is consumed by all three named paths:

- **dispatchd** (`contrib/mac/dispatchd.py`): loads the installed JSON
  projection via `contrib/mac/action_classes.py` (`ACTION_CLASSES_JSON`
  overrides it in tests). A launch is a `write-worktree` action ending in the
  job's publish-phase class (job-id prefixes → `merge`/`close`, default
  `publish`); both must be listed and allowed or the job stays queued
  (`ACTION_CLASS_DENIED` event, `.acdenied` marker, `seen.add`). Reaps only
  spawn `reap-one.sh`/`publish.sh` when the job's class gate is in
  `publishableGates` (`publish-pipeline`, `merge-queue`) — anything else holds
  the worktree (`ACTION_CLASS_HELD`, `.acdenied`, `kept_worktrees`). Batch
  membership and the launch metric (`action_class` field) also consult the
  registry, and `status.json` reports `action_classes.loaded`/`schema`.
- **Leader** (`src/core/vision/leader-apply.ts`): `classifyLeaderAction`
  consults `actionClassDisposition(actionClassForLeaderKind(kind))` before the
  existing grant check — a kind landing in a `forbidden` class is refused (C),
  an `operator`-gated class escalates. The existing A/B/C axis and purity are
  preserved; all four mapped kinds currently resolve `allowed`.
- **publish.sh** (`contrib/mac/publish.sh`): resolves its run mode to an action
  class (`publish` for default mode, `merge` for `--integrated-merge`/
  `--integrated-upstream-*`) via `action_classes.py check`; an unlisted or
  non-publishable class aborts with `RESULT ABORT action-class-<name>-not-publishable`
  before any mutation — in front of every existing gate (git-safe,
  secret-shape, protected paths, G1, fork guard).

Fail closed everywhere: unlisted names resolve to a frozen descriptor
(`gate=forbidden`, `blastRadius=unknown`, `reversibility=irreversible`);
missing/malformed registry files load as `None`/`unlisted`, which denies every
launch and publish. The registry is an additional gate — no existing control
was weakened or removed.

`phm fleet action-classes [--json]` prints the registry for operators
(read-only).

### Digest items addressed

- **Item 7 — unified action-class autonomy registry**: implemented as scoped
  (eight classes, gate + blast-radius + reversibility metadata, single
  registry, dispatchd/Leader/publish consumers, fail-closed for unlisted
  classes).

Note: the digest file itself
(`~/.ashlr-runs/coordination/phantom-productive-20261105/RESEARCH-DIGEST.md`)
could not be read — the environment denied access even after read-scope grants
(TCC). Implementation proceeded from the job brief's explicit item-7
specification and repository architecture; no other digest items were claimed.

  fail-closed resolver, dispositions, job-prefix map, publishable gates,

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE5-INCIDENT-GATE

## Summary

Incident-to-gate hardening (research digest item 8): when a failure class
repeats — the same lane error, the same work failure on a repo+kind, the same
unmerged-PR pattern — the fleet now tightens the gate that owns it instead of
leaving a note. Fixes go into gates, not sticky notes.

New verb `ashlr fleet incident-gate` (dry-run by default, `--apply` to act):

- `src/core/fleet/incident-gate.ts` — pure miner + evaluator + private state.
  Folds bounded `metrics/jobs.jsonl` and `dispatch-events.log` text into
  failure signals for three classes:
  - `lane-error` — autobackoff/autobackoff_skip/authbackoff_skip rows,
    AUTH_FAILURE_SEEN / USAGE_LIMIT_SEEN / MODEL_CAPACITY_SEEN /
    LAUNCH_FAILED / LAUNCH_DEFERRED event lines, finish pool_error /
    failure_class / nonzero exit / empty-diff, task_outcome failed|deferred,
    precheck_skip / precheck_parked → bounded lane hold through the same
    guarded slots.json writer `fleet lane-hold` uses (held_by
    `phantom incident-gate`, ≤ 120 min, refreshable, never overwrites a
    manual hold).
  - `test-failure` — repo+kind-attributed repeats of the same normalized
    failure code → bounded repo `cooldown` hold via `setRepoHold`
    (actor `backpressure`, 6 h — the same cooldown backpressure uses).
  - `merge-conflict` — repeated PRs closed unmerged on one repo (the ledger's
    conflict proxy; reconciler outcome rows are projected exactly like
    `batcher.read_rows` does, repo resolved from the PR URL when absent) →
    the same repo cooldown.
- A class fires once per 3 NEW in-window signals (7 d default,
  `--window-hours` to change) after its `firedAt` watermark — the same
  "N new failures after the last trigger" semantics as backpressure, so
  reruns never double-hold and continued failure re-tightens.
- Every applied/refused decision is appended to
  `~/.ashlr/fleet/incident-gates.jsonl` (0600, O_NOFOLLOW); watermarks live in
  `incident-gate.json` (0600 atomic write in a 0700 dir). Missing/corrupt
  state is the empty state; an unreadable evidence source reports
  `unreadable` and exits 1 — never treated as zero.
- All recorded text is secret-scrubbed and bounded; failure codes are
  normalized to a safe charset before they reach any hold reason.

Built on the autobackoff pattern (contrib/mac/dispatchd.py): detect a
repeated signature, hold the implicated scope for a bounded time, record the
decision. No new architecture, no new dependencies, no security-control
changes — lane holds go through the existing guarded writer and repo
cooldowns reuse the existing `cooldown` hold kind and `backpressure` actor.

body:

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES: RQ-SWE5-FAILRATE-GATE

## Summary
Merge-confidence gate for fleet auto-merge. A pure scorer folds diff-risk
heuristics (`scoreDiffRisk`: size, surface area, test delta), fleet-IQ
durability history (`buildFleetEvalReport`: repo group, falling back to the
fleet-wide rate) and CI state into a 0-100 score. Weights are 50/30/20; missing
evidence is dropped and the weights renormalize, so it is never counted as good
or bad. Default threshold is 55. Below it, or with a hard blocker, the PR is
routed to leader review (existing owner-lane path) instead of auto-merge.

Blockers (force review whatever the score): unmeasurable diff, high diff risk,
failed CI checks, repo/fleet durability lower bound < 0.5 over >= 10 resolved merges.

Wiring (`standing-merge-pass.ts`): after G6, before publishing the PR, score
diff + history; leader-review => `openChangePr(..., ownerLane=true, reason)`.
The score is exposed in PR metadata as a body line:
`Merge confidence: 78/100 (threshold 55) · auto-merge eligible · diff 70 · history 92 · ci —`.
History comes from a new optional dep `evalReport` (default: 30-day report from
`~/.ashlr-runs/metrics/jobs.jsonl` plus signed observations, capped at 32 MiB,
null on any error), read once per pass. CI is not scored at open time because G7
already requires required checks green; the scorer accepts `ci` for callers that have it.

Tuning note: threshold 70 routed plain small untested source changes (score 55)
to review and broke 19 existing merge-flow tests, so default is 55.

# RQ-SWE5-SOL-MERGEQ2

## Summary

Extended the existing overlap-connected-component merge planner and greedy clean-wave ordering with bounded local preparation. `fleet merge-batch --json` now includes the next three eligible SHA-bound preparation specs. Failed upstream reads and unreadable snapshots produce no preparation specs. The exported executor prefetches heads, rejects stale heads, rehearses independent rebases in detached temporary worktrees, and defers overlapping successors until their predecessors land. No PR branch is updated, and no publishing or PR-state commands were run.

The existing cluster/order machinery remains the source of truth rather than introducing another graph implementation. Execution is an explicit scheduler library API; the CLI remains read-only. Hooks, signing, autostash, rebase-merges and ref updates are disabled for rehearsal. Worktrees are cleaned on success and failure. Git diagnostics are withheld.

## Files

- `src/core/fleet/merge-queue-prep.ts`: bounded lookahead specs and local Git executor.
- `src/cli/fleet-merge-batch.ts`: additive JSON preparation projection.
- `test/fleet-merge-queue-prep.test.ts`: six tests covering ordering, bounds, missing evidence, stale identities, dependencies, cleanup and conflict/error classification.
- `docs/FLEET-MERGE-BATCH.md`: snapshot SHA field, scheduler API and reuse rules.
- `BRIDGE_NOTES.md`: handoff and evidence.

## Conflict measurement

Controlled file-overlap fixture: PR 1 touches a/b/c; PRs 2, 3 and 4 each touch one corresponding file. FIFO [1,2,3,4] exposes 3/4 PRs to an earlier overlapping merge (75%). Existing cluster ordering [2,3,4,1] exposes 1/4 (25%): 50 percentage points lower, 66.7% fewer predicted rebases. The test computes both counts. This validates reuse of the existing ordering, not a new improvement over its prior algorithm. Lookahead prepares the three independent leaves and prefetches and defers the hub, avoiding a rebase that would immediately be invalidated.

These are predicted file-overlap rates on a synthetic fixture, NOT observed production Git conflicts. Production before/after rates are unmeasured: this task cannot merge/publish or operate sweeps. Executor conflict classification uses Git's unmerged-index evidence; tests inject its Git adapter, so real-repository rehearsal performance and conflict rates are not claimed.

title: bridge: RQ-DRAIN3-PH-06
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-DRAIN3-PH-06` (pool: devin), single commit on base `65d714ece`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-DRAIN3-PH-06

Rework of conflicting PRs 2912, 2915, 2966, 2983, 3057, 3062 onto current main
(`65d714ec`, release 3.30.26). All changes left uncommitted in the worktree;
publish.sh owns publishing.

## Summary

- **2912** — ported the missing changelog-fragment half of the bundle:
  `src/core/fleet/changelog-fold.ts`, `src/cli/fleet-changelog.ts`
  (`fleet changelog add|fold` over `changelog.d/<id>.<kind>.md`), both test
  suites, and the generated registry entry. Fold targets the live
  `## [Unreleased]` heading (plus the older `## [x.y.z] — Unreleased` form).
  Lane-health, skills, UI, self-tick API/schedule and build-commit pieces of
  the PR were already on main and were not re-ported.
- **2915** — main's `fleet self-tick-check` verifies the service-manager
  schedule; the PR's read-only record probe was merged semantically as a new
  `--record-only` mode (`--require-apply`, `--max-age-seconds`) with
  `checkSelfTickRecord` in core. Never spawns, locks, ticks or writes.
- **2966** — ported opt-in bus progress onto main's newer self-loop:
  `--bus-to/--bus-root/--bus-run-id` (all-or-nothing) posts one compact
  `fleet-self-loop-pass` envelope per completed pass through the existing
  `appendBusInbox` transport. `posted`/`duplicate` count as delivery; any
  other outcome throws into `observer-error` (exit 1) without re-running the
  tick. Bodies carry only kind/runId/pass/exitCode/state/failure/delay
  fields — no reports, paths, stdout or exception text.
- **2983** — ported weekly quota pacing: `usage_verdict`/`lane_admission`
  in dispatchd defer routine claims ahead of a lane's reset window
  (elapsed + 0.10), let P0/critical READY lines spend to 95%, fall back to
  60% on unknown reset, and never block on missing usage. `admission.json`
  v2 gains `lanes`; `phm pool admission --json` mirrors the verdicts via
  `usageVerdict` for both v2 snapshots and legacy probes.
- **3057** — skipped (see below).
- **3062** — ported verified live-parity items: `claude_oauth_expired` and
  `devin_weekly_quota` AB_RX patterns, narrowed `claude_not_logged_in` auth
  pattern (CLI's own line only), `MAX_LAUNCH_PER_TICK` 4→8, `PH_DRIP_MAX`
  150→400, `GITSAFE_SHA` → `234fb12a…` (matches the pin already in
  `contrib/mac/publish.sh` on main). `MAX_REAPS` was dropped: main's reap
  rework removed the constant. `.gitignore` hunk already present.

REWORKS_PR: 2912 — reworked: changelog add/fold fragments ported; rest of bundle already on main.
REWORKS_PR: 2915 — reworked: record-health verdict added as --record-only alongside main's schedule check.
REWORKS_PR: 2966 — reworked: --bus-* group posts compact pass envelopes via appendBusInbox; failures -> observer-error.
REWORKS_PR: 2983 — reworked: weekly pacing verdicts in dispatchd fill loop, admission.json lanes, pool admission mirror.
REWORKS_PR: 3057 — skipped: `phm bus` verb is already owned on main by `phm fleet bus` (threads/tasks/claims/receipts); a second bus.message.v1 store would need an owner-chosen name and overlaps Agent Bus v2 — architectural decision, not a mechanical merge.
REWORKS_PR: 3062 — reworked: live-parity patterns/constants ported; MAX_REAPS moot (constant removed on main), GITSAFE_SHA verified against publish.sh pin.

## Verification

Commands run (all with scratch `HOME=$(mktemp -d)` where applicable):

- `npx vitest run` on touched/affected suites — see counts below.
- `python3 -m unittest` in `contrib/mac/tests` for the dispatchd suites.
- `node scripts/verify-changed.mjs --force` — PASS (file selection, fleet
  registry check, eslint changed files, tsgo --noEmit, realio lane lint,
  verse sync-I/O lint, dedupe).
- `npm run check:docs` — PASS, 0 errors.
- `npm run lint` (full) — 2 errors total: one in this change
  (`no-useless-escape` in self-loop-bus-progress.ts, fixed; changed-files
  eslint now PASS) and one pre-existing on main
  (`src/core/fleet/eval-report.ts:430` `no-dupe-else-if`, untouched by this
  change — flagged for follow-up, not introduced here).
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- Manual smoke: `fleet changelog add|fold [--apply]` against a scratch repo —
  fragment write, dry-run preview and apply+delete all verified.

Pass/fail counts:

- Vitest: 20 files / 221 tests passed, 0 failed
  (8 touched suites: 113 tests; 12 fleet-self-loop regression suites: 108).
- Python `contrib/mac/tests`: test_usage_pacing 4/4, test_dispatchd_patterns
  7/7, test_loadgate 43/43 (one timing flake
  `test_swap_growth_window_and_boundary` under parallel load — passed on
  isolated re-run), test_dispatchd 62/62 after updating two claim-limit
  expectations to the new live-parity cap of 8.
- verify-changed / check:docs / eslint-changed / tsgo: all PASS.

Net LOC: +2241 / −43 across 20 files (10 new files, ~1873 LOC of new
code+tests).

## Notes / risks

- PR 3057 is the only non-rework: the `bus` verb collision is real and the
  fleet bus + Agent Bus v2 already provide messaging with acks/receipts.
  If the owner still wants bus.message.v1, it needs a new verb name
  (e.g. `phm bus-msg`) and a decision on how it relates to Agent Bus v2.
- `usage_verdict`/`usageVerdict` intentionally mirror each other; the
  Python and TS tests pin the same boundary table.
- `GITSAFE_SHA` could not be verified against the live host file from this
  machine, but `contrib/mac/publish.sh` on main already pins the identical
  `234fb12a…` hash for the same file, so the bump aligns dispatchd with the
  repo's own expectation.
- dispatchd's `urgent_jobs` set is computed once per tick from READY router
  lines (`P0|critical`), equivalent to the PR's per-candidate scan but O(1)
  per job.
</details>

body:

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-DRAIN3-PH-01

Rework pass over conflicting PRs 950, 970, 976, 1013, 1022, 1058 in
`ashlr-ai/phantom` onto current `master` (`de42a64958`, fetched 2026-11-08).

All six PR heads share the pre-rebase history root with each other but not with
the squashed/rebased `master` tip available at session start; each PR's net
change was extracted as `git diff <merge-base> <pr-head>` and ported by hand.
The worktree was then fast-forwarded to the then-current `origin/master`
(`git reset --hard origin/master`) and the ported changes reapplied, so the
deliverable sits on today's main, not the stale base.

## Per-PR outcomes

- `REWORKS_PR: 950` — **reworked.** Live queue station graph (RQ-QUEUE-5)
  ported: `queue.stats.v1` schema/validator, rho bands, bottleneck selection,
  fixtures, `queue_now.v1` adapter, pluggable sources and the plain-SVG
  `QueueStationGraph` mounted in `FleetDashboardView`. The PR's ad-hoc
  `localStorage["phantom.flag.agentWorkspace"]` gate was replaced with master's
  landed flag store (`useFeatureFlag('agentWorkspace')` from
  `app/desktop-state.js`, the RQ-DESKTOP-P1-1 mechanism the PR anticipated).
  `command`/`http` sources remain stubs: `phm queue stats --json` on master
  emits the journal-stats schema, not `queue.stats.v1`, so it cannot feed this
  contract without a new producer; stale RQ-QUEUE-3 comments were corrected.
- `REWORKS_PR: 970` — **SUPERSEDED.** Launch-contention intent is already on
  master in evolved form: `scripts/bridge/disk.py` holds kernel `flock`
  worktree leases, launch/publish lifecycle, publication-evidence
  verification and quarantine; `scripts/bridge-clone.py` +
  `scripts/bridge-worktree.mjs` (`requireClone`, lockfile manifest checks)
  cover APFS cloning; `contrib/mac/publish.sh` is the pinned publisher with
  CODEOWNERS/sensitive-path gates. The PR's parallel `scripts/mac-bridge/`
  Python pipeline would duplicate the sanctioned path.
- `REWORKS_PR: 976` — **skipped: needs owner judgment.** 81 files / +11.3k LOC
  landing a parallel coding-cli provider + pool-scheduler + fleet-dashboard
  stack. Its intent (pool scheduling by account headroom/capacity/metered
  class, fleet dashboard, subscription CLI adapters) is substantially covered
  by master's evolved `src/core/routing/` (scheduling, selector,
  subscription-only boundaries, headroom, tiers) and the fleet CLI/web-ui;
  the residual coding-cli spawn/ledger layer would create a second provider
  stack and embeds billing-class/metered opt-in semantics that need an owner
  decision. Too divergent to rework safely in one pass.
- `REWORKS_PR: 1013` — **SUPERSEDED.** `scripts/cycle/collect.mjs` +
  `capture.mjs` implement the same cycle-metrics backfill: `cycle_stage.v1`
  events for the same seven AshlrAI repos, durable JSONL spool, atomic cursor,
  inclusive watermark, `--send`/`--dry-run`, plus `test/cycle-collect*.test.ts`
  recovery coverage. The PR's single-file `cycle-collect.mjs` is an earlier
  iteration of what landed.
- `REWORKS_PR: 1022` — **SUPERSEDED.** Agent Bus v2 (`src/core/fleet/bus-board.ts`
  threads/tasks/deliveries/receipts with TTL + `bus-inbox`, `phm bus
  thread|task` verbs) covers directed send → inbox → ack semantics; master's
  `bus-envelope.ts` is a newer channel-aware superset of the PR's RQ-BUS-1A
  dependency. A parallel `bus-mailbox.ts` would create a second bus silo.
- `REWORKS_PR: 1058` — **reworked.** `phm metrics prod --json` ported as a
  first-class subcommand beside master's existing metrics verbs: new
  `src/cli/metrics-prod.ts` (CliIo convention, test-injectable reads) +
  `src/core/metrics/production.ts` (verbatim collector: paginated GitHub PR /
  release reads, tag→commit resolution, merge-commit ancestry, exact
  npm/crates.io version evidence, unknown-stays-in-denominator), docs
  `PRODUCTION-METRICS.md` + index row, `prod` added to metrics completions and
  both help tables. Test file adapted from the PR's replaced-signature
  `cmdMetrics` to `cmdMetricsProd`, plus a dispatch-level routing test.

## Commands run

- `git fetch origin master`, `git fetch origin pull/<N>/head` for all six PRs;
  per-PR `git diff <merge-base> <head> --stat` to isolate net changes (PR heads
  are merge commits onto pre-rebase master; merge-base = tip's second parent).
- Superseded checks: file existence + content diffs vs `origin/master`
  (`scripts/bridge/disk.py`, `scripts/cycle/`, `src/core/fleet/bus-*.ts`,
  `src/core/routing/`, `src/cli/metrics.ts`, `src/web-ui/data/feature-flags.ts`).
- `npm run install:worktree` (pnpm 10.28.2 shared store) — worktree shipped
  with a partial node_modules; eslint was broken until healed.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/production-metrics.test.ts` —
  **17/17 pass**.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run --config vitest.config.web.ts
  src/web-ui/data/queue-stats src/web-ui/routes/fleet-dashboard` —
  **4 files, 44/44 pass**.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run test:ci -- test/production-metrics.test.ts
  test/doc-facts.test.ts test/m32.help.test.ts` — **all pass**;
  `test/documentation-navigation.test.ts` — **4 failures, pre-existing on
  master** (packaged-docs payload misses `CHAIN-VERIFY.md`,
  `FLEET-MERGE-LATENCY.md`, `FLEET-REBASE-PLAN.md`, `FLEET-VERBS.md`,
  `FLEET-MERGE-BATCH.md`, `CHANNELS.md` — upstream docs/README links ahead of
  package.json `files`; unrelated to this diff, which uses the sanctioned
  github.com source-guide link form).
- `test/cli-registry-drift.test.ts` — **3 failures, pre-existing on master**:
  upstream `chain` command dispatched without completions/help registry
  entries (tune gap already fixed upstream; chain is newer).
- `test/cli-help-no-side-effects.test.ts` — **1120 pass / 13 fail, all

- `cli-help-exit`, `cli-help-safety-core`, `first-run-cli-help`,

  **all pass**.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` (backend) — **clean**; `npx tsc --noEmit -p

- `npx eslint` on all changed/new files — **clean**.
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run check:docs` — **0 errors**.

+1,235 / −3 across 18 files (2 reworked features; no `.github/`, CODEOWNERS,
release-config or secret-surface changes; no new runtime dependencies —
`smol-toml@1.9.0` was already a dependency).

  deadline (same per-reader bound `readUsageResources` uses for this reader).

  never stalls, the work promise carries a `.catch` so a late settle is never
  an unhandled rejection, and a late real result still lands in the reader's
  TTL cache for the next poll.

  refused bytes never reach the view (regression test proves a 0o666 file's

### Broken links found and fixed

1. **`parseResources` ignored the router contract** (`mission-control.ts`). The
   router writes `used_frac` (0..1+, see `fleet-resources.ts`, `dispatchd`), but
   only `weekly_used_pct`-style keys were read — every lane fell to "Time left has
   not reported". `used_frac`/`usedFrac` now parse, clamp at 100% consumed, and a
   `{lanes: {devin: {...}}}` nested map no longer yields a bogus "lanes" row
   (fleet-resources test fixtures show both shapes on disk).

2. **`withDevinUsage` was dead code** — `fleet.resources.devin` was never
   populated, so `/api/resource` always showed the devin pool `unknown`.
   `readResourceView` now accepts an optional `devinRead` dep and merges a live
   custody read (`devin-api-v3-org-cycle`, 5 min TTL / 30 s negative TTL) bounded
   by `DEVIN_READ_BOUND_MS = 4_000`. Wired into `GET /api/resource` and
   `phm status --json`. A slow/hanging/thrown read degrades only the devin lane;
   other pools still project, and reader failure details never reach the wire
   (`source: null`, `pctUsed: null`, `status: 'unknown'`).

3. **Refresh cadence and marks.** `FleetMissionPane` polled at 5 000 ms (not <5 s)
   and Time-left rows were text-only. Now 4 000 ms + the existing `ProviderLogo`
   per lane id via a shared `providerEngine()` mapper (also deduplicated into

   replaced its raw 15 s `setInterval` with `usePollWhileVisible` at 4 s — hidden
   tabs no longer poll.

A zero-ACU-limit devin reading (`acuLimit: 0`, the SWE-2 promo window through
Nov 30) stays `pctUsed: null` → `status: 'unknown'` with the provider `source`
and `resetAt` carried through. No percentage is fabricated; `resource.v1` has no
'free' enum value and adding one would change the wire schema — `unknown` plus
the reported reset date is the honest representation. The mission pane renders
"Time left has not reported · resets 2026-11-30 00:00 UTC" for that shape.

### Known limitation (measured, documented)

`ResourcesBar`'s devin *overview* row (`/api/verse/devin`, org daily consumption)
still polls at `DEVIN_POLL_MS = 60_000` — a deliberately lazy shared provider read
