title: bridge: RQ-SWE3-REBASEORDER-1
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-SWE3-REBASEORDER-1` (pool: devin), single commit on base `addfd8cb2`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE3-REBASEORDER-1: rebase ordering optimizer

## Summary

Rebase jobs now batch by touched-file overlap instead of arbitrary/dominant-directory
grouping: PRs sharing files (transitively) land in the SAME `RQ-BATCH-*` session so one
session resolves the cluster, while disjoint PRs spread across batches.

- `src/core/fleet/rebase-order.ts` (new): `fileClusters` (union-find over shared
  paths; empty file sets stay singletons) + `clusterKey` (`clu-<lowest PR>`).
- `src/core/drive/queuegen.ts`: clusters each repo's open PRs once per cycle over the
  full `QueuegenPr.files` list and stamps `cluster=clu-<n>` on every emitted
  `RQ-REBASE-*` line's attrs (`rebaseLine` gains an optional `cluster` param, so
  the API stays backward compatible). Stamps preserve full-file clustering even
  though a line only shows the truncated conflict list.
- `contrib/mac/rebase_order.py` (new): mirror helper for the restock path —
  `files_from`, `stamped_key`, `clusters`, `assign_areas`, `batch_order` plus a
  stdin/stdout CLI. A stamped `cluster=` acts as one more union edge (pseudo-path
  `#cluster:<key>`, can only merge) and wins as the area key; unstamped lines fall
  back to visible `conflicts="…"`/`file=` paths.
- `contrib/mac/dispatchd.py`: `form_batch` calls `assign_areas` on the candidate
  pool → each rebase task's batching area becomes `rebase:clu-<n>`.
- `contrib/mac/batcher.py`: `rebase:` areas are closed groups — a cluster never
  absorbs orphans and orphans never absorb cluster members — with
  `MIN_REBASE_BATCH = 2` (pairs still win by serializing).
- `contrib/mac/restock.py`: two `RQ-REBASE` lines may share a `(repo, file)` dedupe
  key (the first claimant is recorded; mixed rebase/non-rebase or non-rebase pairs
  still skip `dup-file`).
- `contrib/mac/install.sh` FILES list now ships `rebase_order.py`
  (`test_install.py` updated to match). **Security re-pin required before live
  install — same as every contrib/mac change; not performed here.**
- Docs: `docs/REBASE-ORDERING.md` (convention + helper usage), index entry in
  `docs/README.md`, batch-ordering paragraph in `contrib/mac/README.md`, AGENTS.md
  pointer. Also fixed one pre-existing em dash in AGENTS.md (desktopctl section)
  so `test/agents-md-audit.test.ts` passes on the file this change touches.

## Commands run (all with a temporary HOME)

- `node scripts/verify-changed.mjs` (foreground, once): PASS — file selection,
  eslint changed files, tsgo --noEmit, realio lane lint (WARN: unrelated unchanged
  files listed), verse sync-I/O lint, verify dedupe.
- `npm run typecheck` (tsc --noEmit + web): PASS.
- `eslint` on the 4 changed TS files: clean (eslint `lib/` was pruned from this
  worktree's node_modules; restored from the published 9.39.5 tarball to run it).
- `npm run check:docs`: PASS (0 errors).
- `npx vitest run test/rebase-order.test.ts test/queuegen.test.ts`: 32/32 pass.
- `npx vitest run test/doc-facts.test.ts test/agents-md-audit.test.ts
  test/docs-readme-links.test.ts test/docs-markdown-lane.test.ts`: 73/73 pass.
- `python3 -B -m unittest contrib/mac/tests/test_rebase_order.py`: 25/25 pass.
- `python3 -B -m unittest contrib/mac/tests/test_restock.py`: 35/35 pass.
- `python3 -B -m unittest contrib/mac/tests/test_batcher.py`,
  `test_batching.py`, `test_install.py`: 16 + 5 + 8 pass (earlier run).
- `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s contrib/mac/tests -p "test_dispatchd.py"`:
  56/56 pass.
- `python3 -B contrib/mac/rebase_order.py --size 4` on 3 fixture rows: correct
  clusters/areas JSON.

## Known issues / limitations

- `test/docs-index-source-only-links.test.ts` fails on base AND on this branch:
  docs/README.md already linked 7 docs outside the curated package; the new
  REBASE-ORDERING.md entry is the 8th. Pre-existing failure class, unchanged.
- Clustering sees only PRs in the generator's listing (files list caps at 100
  paths; conflicts list at 8 on the line): truncation can only under-cluster,
  never wrongly merge — documented in docs/REBASE-ORDERING.md.
- Live dispatcher unchanged: `install.sh` needs the Security sha-pin refresh
  before `--json` install; tests use synthetic `~/.ashlr-runs` fixtures only.
- `contrib/mac/host-integration/dispatchd.candidate.py` is a stale separate
  lineage; intentionally untouched.

## Net LOC

+790 / −17 (tracked: +129/−17 across 11 files; new files: +661 code+tests,
+81 docs README/REBASE-ORDERING.md … exact new-file wc: rebase_order.py 219,
test_rebase_order.py 293, REBASE-ORDERING.md 81, rebase-order.ts 54,
rebase-order.test.ts 31). No commits made; worktree left dirty as instructed.

title: bridge: RQ-SWE3-IMSGDEEP-1
body:
Automated bridge job `RQ-SWE3-IMSGDEEP-1` (pool: devin), single commit on base `addfd8cb2`.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE3-IMSGDEEP-1

iMessage depth for the teammate bridge: chunked PATCH transfer reassembly
with sha256 verification, findings mirroring onto `teammate.findings`, and
rowid dedup with watermark advancement past expired rows.

Base: `master` (worktree `wt/RQ-SWE3-IMSGDEEP-1`, branch
`codex-bridge/RQ-SWE3-IMSGDEEP-1`). All changes are **uncommitted** in the
worktree; no commit, push, tag, PR or gh write was performed.

## Stacked dependency

DOTFEED-1 (`49001f9c0`) and DOTFEED-TTL (`411b6aef7`) are in-flight sibling
bridges — neither is on `master`. Their `imessage-findings-bridge.ts` +
test + doc lines were applied as the base layer (the bridge this job
extends), matching how prior stacked iMessage jobs carried in-flight deps.
Everything else in this diff is new.

## What changed

**New — `src/core/comms/imessage-patch-transfer.ts` (499 LOC).**
`PATCH-BEGIN <id> <parts> <sha256>` / `PATCH-PART <id> <i>/<parts>` /
`PATCH-END <id> <sha256>` protocol for the personal Codex dot.

- `parsePatchFrame(text)`: pure grammar check; `null` for ordinary texts,
  `'malformed'` for a marker that fails to parse. Bounds: id
  `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}`, ≤ 64 parts, frame ≤ 16 KiB.
- `recordPatchFrame(msg, opts)`: consumes one allowlisted non-Mason intake
  row. Durable per-transfer state under
  `<imessage>/patches/open/<id>.json` (dir `0700`, files `0600`, atomic
  writes, serialized by the local-store lock). Rejects: malformed frames,
  secret-shaped chunks (scrubbed ≠ verbatim ⇒ refused, never partially
  recorded), spent ids, id conflicts, cross-sender frames, part-count or
  chunk conflicts, > 8 open transfers, > 512 KiB payloads, END hash ≠
  BEGIN hash. Every outcome is terminal for its rowid: a 512-entry handled
  ring + monotonic `lastRowid` watermark in `patches/state.json` make a
  re-poll a `duplicate`, never a re-apply.
- Assembly is in-order over the declared part indexes; sha256 is verified
  over the concatenated UTF-8 payload **before** the artifact write —
  verified payloads land at `patches/<id>.patch`, receipts beside them at
  `<id>.receipt.json` (counts, ids, hashed sender — never text or handles).
  A rejected/expired id is spent forever; the sender must pick a fresh id.
- `sweepPatchTransfers(opts)`: one bounded pass per poll expires open
  transfers older than 6 h (also reaps corrupt open files as
  `corrupt-state` rejects) and advances the watermark past their rowids,
  so expired frames can never be resurrected.
- `readPatchReceipts(opts)`: bounded listing (newest 64 by mtime) feeding
  the findings bridge's artifact announcements.
- Every entry point never throws; ledger failures return `'unavailable'`
  and the caller defers the batch for retry — never a silent reset.

**Tests:** no test command

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# Bridge notes — RQ-SWE3-AUTOPILOT-1

Closed-loop fleet autopilot: `phm fleet autopilot --once --json` — one bounded,
read-only planning cycle that (1) reads queue/slots/admission state, (2)
computes lane utilization vs targets, (3) identifies the single
highest-leverage gap and (4) emits exactly one proposed action as JSON.
Never mutates — the proposal is advisory for the leader-as-CEO loop.

## What changed

- `src/core/fleet/autopilot.ts` (new): `readFleetAutopilotState` assembles the
  four inputs — `queue/status.json` via `explainFleetAdmission`,
  `queue/ready.tsv` + `metrics/jobs.jsonl` via `readFleetQueue`,
  `queue/slots.json` via `readLaneTargets`, and an opt-in `--repo`
  rebase-coverage read via `readRebaseStatus` (read-only `gh pr list`).
  Each source degrades independently; nothing throws. `planFleetAutopilot`
  is the pure planner: joins lanes across the three local sources into
  running/target/queued/ready/parked/held/freeSlots/utilization, emits a
  ranked `gaps[]` list, and maps the top gap to one action.
- `src/cli/fleet-autopilot.ts` (new): `cmdFleetAutopilot` — thin argv parse
  (`--once`, `--json`, `--runs-dir <abs>`, repeatable `--repo <owner/name>`),
  calls the reader + planner, prints `fleet.autopilot.v1` JSON or a human
  summary. Convention-resolved via the registry; `fleet verbs` infers
  `effect: 'read'`.
- `src/core/fleet/runs-parked-queue.ts`: opt-in `depDetail` flag emits
  `metDeps` — PARKED-DEP rows whose DEPENDENCY GATE ids are all MERGED but
  were never unparked (the "stale parked deps" signal; the unpark pass
  missed them). Same bounded prompt read as `unmetDeps`, no extra I/O.
  Default output is byte-identical for existing callers.
- `src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts`: regenerated
  (`scripts/gen-fleet-registry.mjs`).
- `src/cli/completions.ts`: added `autopilot` to the fleet verb list
  (doc-facts requires documented verbs to be completable).
- `docs/FLEET-VERBS.md` + `AGENTS.md`: documented the verb.
- `test/fleet-autopilot.test.ts` (new): 30 tests — pure planner (all four
  gap kinds, severity ranking, every action shape), injected-reader state
  assembly, CLI arg handling, `depDetail`/`metDeps`, and two end-to-end
  runs over a fixture runs dir (real `readFleetAutopilotState`).

## Proposal contract

`action` is one of: `enqueue` (`type: 'rebase'|'restock'|'unpark'`, count,
lane/repos), `hold-lane` (an over-deep lane pausing so a starved lane can
reach the cap), or `no-op` (`fleet-healthy` | `capacity-bound` |
`dispatch-stall` | `state-unreadable`). Severity order:
uncovered-conflicts > starved-lane > stale-parked-deps > missing-restock,
with an explicit kind tie-break; `status` reports ok/degraded/unreadable
from source health.

- `node scripts/verify-changed.mjs` — PASS (file selection, fleet registry

- `./node_modules/.bin/eslint` on the 4 touched TS files — clean

  30 pass / 0 fail
- Related suites under `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run`:
  parked-queue + consumers (12 files) 115 pass / 0 fail; doc/verb/admission/
  supply/lane-target/rebase suites (11 files) 121 pass / 0 fail;
  autopilot+doc-facts+verbs (5 files) 81 pass / 0 fail;
  completion suites (2 files) 34 pass / 0 fail
- Smoke: `npx tsx src/cli/index.ts fleet autopilot --once --json
  --runs-dir <fixture>` and `--help`, `fleet verbs --grep autopilot` —
  correct JSON, human summary, usage and `effect: 'read'`

Environment note: `npm run install:worktree` (pnpm 10.28.2, shared store)
was run first — the worktree's node_modules was a partial install (eslint
lib absent).

## Net LOC

+900 / −9 (net +891) across 8 files, excluding this notes file: 873 in the
three new files, +27/−9 in the five modified files (+9 net in
runs-parked-queue.ts).

## Limits / follow-ups

- The conflicting-PR gap class needs `--repo` (one bounded `gh pr list`
  per repo, read-only); without it `sources.rebase` is `unconfigured` and
  the class is unmeasured, not guessed.
- `--once` is a marker only; a future `--watch`/interval mode can share
  `planFleetAutopilot` unchanged.
- Actions are proposals; nothing executes them yet. Wiring the leader loop
  to consume `fleet.autopilot.v1` is the intended next step.

## Summary

Leader-as-CEO heartbeat: every Leader tick now records a structured
`fleet.leader-board.v1` board at `~/.ashlr-runs/coordination/leader-board.json`,
and `phm fleet board [--json]` surfaces it. The board is the observability
backbone for autonomous operation:

- **lanes** — per-lane ready / parked / running / merges-last-hour / oldest
  wait, from the existing `getLaneQueueCounts()` reader.
- **queueDepthByTier** — READY rows in `queue/ready.tsv` grouped by normalized
  tier (`frontier|work|mid|fast`; invalid/missing fold into `unknown`), bounded
  at 16 keys. Parked rows are excluded before parsing — a PARKED cell in the
  positional slot would otherwise parse as a bogus READY row and inflate depth.
- **mergesLastHour** — trailing-hour merge total from the same counts reader.
- **conflictingPrs** — distinct PR count + delta/trend/history. Local proxy:
  queuegen emits `RQ-REBASE-<REPO>-<pr>-<sha7>` jobs only for PRs GitHub reports
  DIRTY, so a distinct-PR count over raw ready.tsv (both parked encodings
  scanned) is the fleet's honest view of PRs sitting in conflicts — no `gh`,
  no network. History is bounded at 96 samples; when the current count is
  unmeasured the board reports `delta: null, trend: "unknown"` rather than
  trending stale samples.
- **needsMason** — status/count/items (≤10) from `readNeedsMason`.
- **sources** — per-input health (`healthy|missing|degraded`,
  `ok|unavailable`), so consumers can tell "zero" from "unknown".

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE3-CONFLICPRED-1

## Task

Conflict predictor: given the set of open PRs and recent merge velocity,
predict which open PRs will conflict with the NEXT N merges (file-overlap +
recency heuristic). Expose as `phm fleet conflict-risk --json` feeding the
rebase scheduler: high-risk PRs get rebased proactively before their turn.
Read-only, `src/core/fleet`, thin CLI.

## What landed

- **`src/core/fleet/conflict-risk.ts`** (new, ~595 LOC) — `fleet.conflict-risk.v1`
  report builder. Two bounded `gh pr list` reads (open rows carry
  `FLEET_PR_GH_VIEW_FIELDS,createdAt,title,files`; merged page carries
  `number,files,mergedAt`, sorted `sort:updated-desc`) plus the jobs ledger.
  Reuses `parseFleetPrGhState`, `planMergeBacklog` (predicted merge order:
  green-ready → behind → non-draft pending, oldest-waiting per tier),
  `readMergeBacklogStates`, `normalizeRepoPath`, `scrubSecrets`.
  Heuristic: a predicted merge threatens an open PR on literal file overlap
  (window members only by *earlier* positions); a shared path the base rewrote
  inside the hot window weighs double; each threatening merge contributes
  `min(1, (hot*2+cold)/4)`; score = `1 - Π(1-l)`; bands high ≥ 0.6 /
  medium ≥ 0.3 / low > 0 / none; only `high` sets `rebaseRecommended`.
  Velocity = merges/hour over `--window-hours` (merged page first — all merges
  churn the base — ledger `MERGED` outcomes as fallback); horizon =
  `next / mergesPerHour` sizes the hot window (fallback 24 h, clamp 1–168 h).
  Every leg degrades honestly: `open-failed` / `truncated` sources, per-read
  `reads` flags, `velocity.source`, `counts.unreadable`, `risksOmitted`;
  already-conflicting PRs are listed separately (recut, not rebase).

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

# RQ-SWE3-ATTEMPT-RACE-1 — fix teammate-review finding on PR #4005 (observability)

## Summary

PR #4005 head `14685bce6` adds the `fleet.agent-activity.v1` projection
(`src/core/fleet/agent-activity.ts` + `ashlr fleet activity` + `GET
/api/fleet/activity`). Its fold gated terminal rows only on the attempt's
`launch` timestamp, so a delayed `finish`/`publish`/`outcome` row stamped in an
older attempt — appended to `metrics/jobs.jsonl` after a requeue but carrying
an older `ts` — advanced the requeued job before relaunch (queued job shown
`finished`/`published`/`merged` ahead of its next launch).

Fix, per the finding: the later queue/launch time is the attempt boundary. A
new `Attempt.boundary` field tracks `max(queue, launch)` timestamps for the
current attempt (queue rows while running count — a requeue moves the boundary
forward even when it does not reset a non-terminal attempt); `finish`,
`publish` and `outcome`/`task_outcome` rows are now admitted only when
`ev.ts >= boundary`. Rows stamped before it stay with the older attempt and
can no longer close, publish or finish the newest one. Stragglers still reach
`timeline`/`mergeMeta`, so the observed history is unchanged — only stage
fields are gated.

## Delta vs reviewed head 14685bce6

`src/core/fleet/agent-activity.ts`: +`boundary` field (`-Infinity` initial),
`Math.max` update on every queue/launch event after the reset check, and the
three terminal gates switched from `a.launched ?? -Infinity`/`a.launched` to
`a.boundary` (the `publish` gate keeps its `ev.ts >= a.finished` arm when a
finish exists, which already implies the boundary). Header and outcome-branch
comments updated to document the boundary.

`test/fleet-activity.test.ts`: three new regressions under
`summarizeAgentActivity` — delayed `outcome` (stays `queued`, and a
post-boundary `CLOSED` on a live attempt still lands), delayed `finish` after
requeue-while-running (stays `running`), delayed `publish` after a terminal
attempt's requeue (stays `queued`, `url` withheld).

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-SWE3-DOTFEED-TTL-1

Pool: devin · Tier: work · Repo: ashlrai/phantom · Base: worktree HEAD `5344526f3`
Task: fix teammate-review findings on PR #4010 (dotbridge findings ingestion,
reviewed head `49001f9c`).

## What is in the worktree

The full PR #4010 diff (`ac173499c..49001f9c`, applied cleanly with
`git apply --3way`) plus the review fixes, left uncommitted as one focused
change. Files: `src/core/comms/imessage-findings-bridge.ts` (new),
`src/core/comms/imessage-inbox-bridge.ts`, `src/cli/imessage.ts`,
`test/imessage-findings-bridge.test.ts` (new),
`test/imessage-teammate-ingest.test.ts`, `docs/IMESSAGE.md`,
`docs/AGENT-BUS.md`.

## Finding 1 — expired findings revive with a fresh 7-day TTL

`readTeammateTexts({sinceMs})` treats `sinceMs` as an **age duration**: a row
is dropped when `now - at > sinceMs`. The reviewed bridge read the inbox with
no age bound at all, so any durable row past the watermark was posted —
including a 30-day-old one (confirmed by the reviewer with a synthetic row).
Because `appendBusInbox` stamps `receivedAt = now` and the envelope carries
`ttl: CHANNEL_BUS_TTL_MS` (7d), posting an expired row revives it on the bus
for another 7 days.

Fix: `bridgeTeammateFindings` now checks each candidate's age inside the pass
(`nowMs - Date.parse(row.at) > CHANNEL_BUS_TTL_MS`); an expired row is never
posted — it is terminal like a refusal, counted `refused` ("rows that can
never be enveloped") and advanced past.

Deliberately **not** done via `sinceMs`: the read must stay unbounded so the
pass still SEES expired rows — filtering them inside `readTeammateTexts`
would hide them from the watermark and re-scan them forever (finding 2). The
`sinceMs` duration-vs-`now−TTL` hazard is documented on
`bridgeTeammateFindings` so a future caller cannot reintroduce it.

## Finding 2 — advance the watermark past expired rows

Expired rows now set `handled = row.rowid`, so `findings-bridge.json`
advances over them exactly like refused rows: they are counted once in
`examined`/`refused`, never left in `pending`, and no later pass re-examines
them.

## Regression tests (match the described scenarios)

Added to `test/imessage-findings-bridge.test.ts`:

1. `never revives an expired finding: a row older than the bus TTL is
   refused, not posted` — seeds a 30-day-old row plus a fresh row; asserts
   `posted: 1, refused: 1` and that the bus holds only the fresh envelope.
2. `advances the watermark past expired rows so no later pass rescans them` —
   a 30-day-old row: `posted: 0, refused: 1, lastRowid: 11`; a second pass
   examines nothing; a fresh row arriving later bridges normally.

Both tests verified to FAIL against the reviewed head (2 failed / 17 passed)
and PASS on the fix — real regression coverage.
